details.label: Summary
details.text: Locally damaging wind may continue through the early evening

details.label: Discussion
details.text: Extensive deep convection is ongoing from southeast GA into parts of the Carolinas, which earlier produced scattered reports of wind damage through the afternoon. While storm organization has generally been limited by weak to modest deep-layer shear, a relatively vigorous line is ongoing east of Charlotte to Greensboro, NC. A narrow plume of moderate buoyancy in advance of this line will continue to support a short-term wind-damage threat. However, the longevity of the threat with this line may be limited by the relatively cooler and less unstable conditions downstream, due to earlier convection and related outflow. Otherwise, sporadic wind damage remains possible from southeast GA into eastern SC< where deep-layer shear is weak, but a corridor of warmer temperatures and steeper low-level lapse rates will remain in place through early evening, in advance of ongoing storms

details.label: Summary
details.text: The area is being monitored for an increase in severe-thunderstorm potential. The primary concerns are large hail and severe wind gusts. A watch issuance is possible

details.label: Discussion
details.text: Isolated thunderstorms are evolving along a SE/NW-oriented confluence axis extending from parts of northwest NE toward the Black Hills. This activity is potentially being aided by a subtle midlevel impulse cresting the ridge in the northern Plains. The UNR 18Z sounding sampled steep deep-layer lapse rates and a long/mostly straight hodograph (around 40 kt of effective shear) -- which will support splitting supercell structures and organized clusters. The primary concern will be large hail and robust outflow/severe wind gusts. Given the subtle large-scale forcing for ascent and some lingering low-level inhibition, storm coverage is uncertain. Convective trends will be monitored in the near term, and a watch issuance is possible

details.label: Summary
details.text: The threat for a few severe wind gusts up to 70-80 mph is expected to increase by mid to late afternoon. A watch is not expected due to the isolated nature of the threat

details.label: Discussion
details.text: Subtle mid-level disturbances embedded in a moist, southerly flow regime are contributing to a gradual increase in thunderstorms this afternoon across portions of central and southern NV. Modification of the 18Z LKN sounding for hotter surface conditions currently observed over northeast NV into northwest UT yields MUCAPE of 500-750 J/kg atop a 3-4 km deep, well-mixed boundary layer. As such, thunderstorms are expected to move/develop north through the region this afternoon into evening with an associated risk for locally severe wind gusts up to 70-80 mph, driven by strong evaporational cooling potential in the sub-cloud layer. Explicit wind gust fields from the latest CAM data continue to highlight portions of north-central and northeast NV into southwest ID as a most likely corridor for the strongest gusts to occur
